reasons: The cited clause (Section 16.2) grants an Array indemnity only for Array's own Array-Territory commercialization, its own clinical studies and breach of the Article 15 reps; it contains no indemnity for Third Party claims that the licensed Products infringe or misappropriate Third Party IP. Under the rule's detection guidance ('Deviation if ... Vendor's indemnity excludes IP infringement') and the fallback (which expressly requires a Vendor IP indemnity with usual exclusions), the clause fails the fallback on a material term, so 'deviation' is the correct classification rather than compliant-at-fallback.

Section 11.4(a) corroborates the gap by placing defence of 'Infringement Actions' on the Subject Party at its own expense, i.e. Ono bears its own costs for infringement claims on Array-licensed technology; the knowledge-qualified, Effective-Date-only Article 15 reps do not close it, and the rationale correctly explains this.

The redline is a targeted insertion of a new limb (e) into the existing 16.2 list, with the customary modification/combination carve-outs and a 'notwithstanding Section 11.4' override to resolve the conflict; the existing gross negligence/willful misconduct exception is preserved and the 'and' is repositioned grammatically. The high changed-character ratio reflects the length of the required insertion, not an unnecessary rewrite.

The failed 'IP infringement indemnity present' regex is a phrasing artefact — the inserted text does create an Array indemnity for Third Party claims alleging infringement/misappropriation; the only shortfall (no express 'defend' verb, no general gross negligence/willful misconduct limb) is a minor sub-element correctly noted in the rationale rather than separately flagged.

Comment is accurate, concise, in first person plural, cites the playbook position and explains both the change and the Section 11.4 problem; no double-flagging of the same commercial term is apparent.
